title: FW↔MLOPS-001: Signed Model Artifact + On-Device OTA Verification
description: The MLOps Engineer provides the OTA (Over-the-Air)-ready model artifact (TFLite Micro binary), its compatibility manifest (model version, target hardware ID, firmware compatibility range, tensor-arena size, flash-budget-check result), the MLOps artifact signature, and a flash-budget-fit confirmation; the Firmware Engineer provides the OTA image format specification (MCUboot-compatible layout, manifest header, signing envelope), the on-device bundling and verification mechanism (A/B partition slot, signature-chain verification, SHA-256 hash validation), device-side compatibility constraints (hardware-ID match, firmware-version-range check, flash-budget check), and on-device inference resource measurements (tensor-arena usage, flash consumption, inference latency). Grounded in MLOPS_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.3 and FIRMWARE_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.11. This is an OTA-chain, security-critical contract: model signing and signature-chain verification are baseline controls (ESC-SEC); FC-026 (model anti-rollback weaker than firmware anti-rollback) requires a per-model monotonic version counter on-device.

model_artifact_delivery.description: MLOPS→FW: signed OTA-ready model artifact + compatibility manifest + flash-budget fit.

artifact_signature.description: MLOps signature (Vault-referenced key material; never a literal secret).

firmware_ota_verification.description: FW→MLOPS: OTA image format, on-device verification, compatibility check, inference measurements, anti-rollback.

anti_rollback_monotonic_counter_ok.description: Per-model monotonic version counter check (FC-026 mitigation).

x-macp.tier_rationale: The signed-model-artifact ↔ on-device-verification edge is part of the OTA closed loop and sits behind permanent HITL gates: model signing and signature-chain verification are baseline controls, and a flash-budget FAIL blocks dispatch. ESC-SEC applies (Security Engineer owns binding signing/anti-rollback decisions); FC-026 anti-rollback is an open residual-risk control.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER + SLA_FROM_EVENT (artifact-format alignment at planning; model-artifact handoff + on-device verification during development; compatibility verification before fleet rollout)
confirm_conditions: the model artifact carries a signature, a 64-hex SHA-256, and a compatibility manifest with flash_budget_check_result = PASS
on-device verification confirms signature_chain_verified = true and sha256_validated = true
tensor-arena, flash, and latency measurements carry explicit units
the per-model monotonic anti-rollback counter is checked (FC-026 mitigation)
reject_conditions: a model artifact dispatched with flash_budget_check_result = FAIL (OCM gate — blocks OTA dispatch)
an artifact accepted with signature_chain_verified = false or an invalid SHA-256 (security baseline — ESC-SEC; Security veto)
a key/secret emitted as a literal value rather than a Vault reference, or anti-rollback bypassed (FC-026; weakens the baseline)
counter_conditions: ALWAYS escalate ESC-SEC when the coordination touches model signing / signature-chain / anti-rollback — propose, do not auto-confirm; the Security Engineer owns the binding decision
the firmware-compatibility range excludes the device's current firmware — request a compatible artifact or a firmware update path before dispatch
